doc.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal Interview, 1962-05-24

chapter: Photographs of the Creole Fiesta and family
title: Block dance postcard, 1960, and the first street block dance
summary: A card for a May 1960 block dance at the Wonderful Boys Home and the first street block dance with food booths.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you about this postcard. Let's see, we've got on here that you were having a meeting, and you were going to have a block dance Friday, May the 6th, 1960, at 1660 North Miro?
What's that, the Wonderful Boys? Mrs. Wonderful Boys.
Yes, at the Wonderful Boys Home. Yes, right. That's right.
You had a block dance right in front of it.

Mrs. Well, it was to be in front, but with the rain we had it inside, indoors. Mrs. Indoors, because of, well, we had, our first block dance was here. Mrs. On the street, yeah. Mrs. On the street. Mrs. On the street. Mrs. On the street. And the city blocked off the street. Johnson and Praia, and they put boots on both sides of the street and we had a lot of doors. Mrs. So that we can sell our wares. Mrs. One was the ice cream booth. Mrs. The hot dog booth. Mrs. What else? Mrs. Hot dog, barbecue booth. Mrs. And different booths. Mrs. And I said, the Holy Family girls danced, the square dance in the street. Mrs. Now these are different pictures of myself. Is it all right to talk about this? Sure. Mrs. All right. Now this is the first, this is the first parade and our first affair here. Mrs. Edna Vivala Serena Senegal. And the gown she wore in her patio. Now this is my umbrella. They say when I put my umbrella out in the patio and all the fixtures, it makes it so much different. And that was taken in my patio. You know, that's, and this is the first gown I wore. Mrs. And this is the second parade. Mrs. And this is the third. It's kind of dark. And this is the fourth. And this is a beautiful gown. Isn't it beautiful?
It's got a train on the back. Mrs. Oh yeah, it has a train, yeah.
